   - The function `__cpuid_entry_get_reg` has been updated to accept a `u32` type for the `reg` parameter instead of a pointer to `struct cpuid_reg`.
   - The switch statement inside this function has been modified to use the `reg` directly.
   - **Original Function Signature:**
     ```c
     static __always_inline u32 *__cpuid_entry_get_reg(struct kvm_cpuid_entry2 *entry, const struct cpuid_reg *cpuid)
     ```
   - **Modified Function Signature:**
     ```c
     static __always_inline u32 *__cpuid_entry_get_reg(struct kvm_cpuid_entry2 *entry, u32 reg)
     ```
   - Similar changes were made in the `cpuid_entry_get_reg` and `guest_cpuid_get_register` functions to pass the `reg` directly instead of a pointer.

The modifications in both files are interconnected as they address the same issue related to the handling of CPU registers in the KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine) code. The change in `cpuid.c` reflects the new way of accessing the CPU register by directly using the `reg` value instead of a pointer to a structure. This change is necessary to avoid triggering a `BUILD_BUG()` when the code is compiled with alignment sanitization enabled (CONFIG_UBSAN). The updates in `cpuid.h` ensure that all functions that interact with CPU registers are consistent with this new approach, thereby improving compatibility and stability when building with specific compiler flags.

Here is the commit message:
KVM: x86: Fix BUILD_BUG() in __cpuid_entry_get_reg() w/
 CONFIG_UBSAN=y

Take the target reg in __cpuid_entry_get_reg() instead of a pointer to a
struct cpuid_reg.  When building with -fsanitize=alignment (enabled by
CONFIG_UBSAN=y), some versions of gcc get tripped up on the pointer and
trigger the BUILD_BUG().

Reported-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Fixes: d8577a4c238f8 ("KVM: x86: Do host CPUID at load time to mask KVM cpu caps")
Fixes: 4c61534aaae2a ("KVM: x86: Introduce cpuid_entry_{get,has}() accessors")
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <sean.j.christopherson@intel.com>
Message-Id: <20200325191259.23559-1-sean.j.christopherson@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by passing a pointer to a `struct cpuid_reg` to the `__cpuid_entry_get_reg()` function, which led to issues when compiling with the `-fsanitize=alignment` flag. Some versions of GCC had trouble with the pointer, triggering the `BUILD_BUG()` macro due to alignment problems. The fix involved changing the function to accept the register value directly instead of a pointer, thus avoiding the alignment issue.

Here is the patch:
 
 static __always_inline u32 *__cpuid_entry_get_reg(struct kvm_cpuid_entry2 *entry,
-						  const struct cpuid_reg *cpuid)
+						  u32 reg)
 {
-	switch (cpuid->reg) {
+	switch (reg) {
 	case CPUID_EAX:
 		return &entry->eax;
 	const struct cpuid_reg cpuid = x86_feature_cpuid(x86_feature);
 
-	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, &cpuid);
+	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, cpuid.reg);
 }
 
 		return NULL;
 
-	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, &cpuid);
+	return __cpuid_entry_get_reg(entry, cpuid.reg);
 }
